findings.source_quote: φοβερῶν ἰδεῶν δοκῶν ἀπαλλάσσειν ὑμῶν τὰς ψυχάς, φοβερωτέρᾳ ἰδέᾳ τὸν ἑκάστου ὑμῶν ἐνθουσιᾶν ποιεῖ νοῦν
findings.english_quote: while seeming to free your souls from fearsome ideas, makes each of your minds possessed by a more fearsome idea
findings.issue: The repeated ἰδέα belongs to the passage’s sustained form-and-image vocabulary: visible idols, imagined forms, and the introduction of God in a form. Unqualified modern English “ideas” obscures this visual force by suggesting abstract thoughts or propositions. A mental-conception reading is possible, but the draft neither explains that choice nor preserves the form/image alternative.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare and revise toward “while seeming to free your souls from fearsome images, makes each of your minds possessed by a more fearsome image.” Add a source-quoted note explaining that ἰδέα can denote a form or appearance, including a mental representation, and that “images” preserves the visual thread without asserting that these are physical statues. Submit the revised wording for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἀγαθὸν δὲ εἰπὼν οὐκέτι ἐκεῖνον λέγει τὸν δίκαιον
findings.english_quote: In saying good, he does not mean that just one
findings.issue: The draft preserves a negative but drops the additional force of οὐκέτι: “no longer,” or logically “not now/under that designation.” The Greek distinguishes what follows when “good” is used, rather than supplying only an unqualified denial.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “But when he says ‘good,’ he no longer means that just one.” If necessary, explain in a source-quoted note that “no longer” can express the logical consequence of using this designation, rather than necessarily alleging a chronological change of belief.

findings.source_quote: τῷ ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ δικαίῳ ὁραθέντι Νῶε
findings.english_quote: to Noah, whom he saw to be righteous
findings.issue: The chosen predicative reading of δικαίῳ is defensible, but an attributive reading also deserves disclosure: “to righteous Noah, whom he saw.” The existing note explains the chosen reading and rejects an inversion into Noah seeing God, but that inversion is not the relevant grammatical alternative. The actual uncertainty concerns whether righteousness is what God perceived or an epithet of Noah.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the proposed main reading only with an expanded source-quoted note preserving “to righteous Noah, whom he saw” as the attributive alternative and explaining why the draft takes δικαίῳ predicatively. Both readings retain Noah as the person seen by God; neither requires correcting the supplied Greek.

findings.source_quote: ἐνίοτε γὰρ ἄλλαις φωναῖς τῶν ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν φοβερὸν καὶ δίκαιον συνίστησι θεὸν
findings.english_quote: For sometimes, in other statements drawn from the scriptures, he establishes a fearsome and just God
findings.issue: The draft treats τῶν ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν as partitive: other statements among those derived from the scriptures. That is a defensible construction, but the genitive can also mark comparison after ἄλλαις: statements different from those derived from the scriptures. This materially changes the attribution of the statements. No note identifies the construction, preserves the comparative alternative, or explains the selected reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explicitly identifying the main text’s partitive interpretation, preserving the alternative “For sometimes, with statements different from those from the scriptures, he presents a fearsome and just God,” and supplying a contextual reason for the choice. Alternatively, propose the comparative rendering as a revision and preserve the partitive reading in its note. Either revised presentation requires fresh review; the supplied print does not need correction merely because these interpretations compete.
